title: Interfacial Charge Transfer and Morphology Govern Magnetism in Ultrathin VOx/MoSe2 Heterostructures
authors: Yasinthara Wadumesthri, Nalaka Kapuruge, Raphael B. de Oliveira, Bruno Ipaves, Guilherme S. L. Fabris, Kinga Lasek, Florence A. Nugera, Jianjun Pan, Xiaomei Jiang, Douglas S. Galvão, Humberto Rodríguez Gutiérrez
abstract: Engineering magnetism in two-dimensional semiconductors through interfacial interactions offers an attractive alternative to substitutional doping and provides opportunities for integrating magnetic and optoelectronic functionality within the same heterostructure. Here, we investigate ultrathin VOx films deposited on monolayer MoSe2 and demonstrate a pronounced enhancement of the magnetic response upon formation of the VOx/MoSe2 interface. Combined structural, spectroscopic, magnetic, and first-principles analyses support a consistent picture in which finite VOx clusters possess intrinsic magnetic moments that are further enhanced by electron transfer from MoSe2 to the oxide. The predicted charge transfer is also consistent with the increased trion contribution observed in the photoluminescence response of the heterostructure. Beyond this interfacial enhancement, the magnetic behavior is strongly governed by the morphology of the ultrathin oxide. A crossover from discontinuous clusters to more continuous films produces qualitatively different temperature dependences: the continuous-film regime exhibits conventional thermal demagnetization and coercive softening, whereas the clustered regime displays an unusual increase in magnetization and nonmonotonic coercivity with increasing temperature. These contrasting responses are captured by a phenomenological model in which morphology determines the collective magnetic dynamics through a distribution of effective reversal barriers and their thermally activated accessibility. Together, the results establish a unified picture in which interfacial charge transfer enhances the local magnetic moments of VOx, while nanoscale morphology governs their collective magnetic dynamics, providing complementary routes for controlling magnetism in oxide/transition-metal dichalcogenide heterostructures.
summary: This work investigates how magnetism can be controlled in VOx/MoSe2 heterostructures by engineering the interface. The authors show that charge transfer from MoSe2 enhances the local magnetic moments of the oxide, while the physical morphology of the oxide layer controls the overall collective magnetic response. This establishes a dual control mechanism for designing next-generation 2D spintronic devices.
main_problem: The study aims to engineer magnetism in 2D semiconductors by utilizing interfacial interactions, offering an alternative to traditional substitutional doping methods.
main_result: The magnetic response is governed by two factors: interfacial charge transfer enhances local magnetic moments in the oxide, while the oxide's morphology dictates the collective magnetic dynamics (e.g., conventional vs. unusual temperature dependence).
method: The research combines experimental characterization (structural, spectroscopic, magnetic measurements) with first-principles theoretical calculations (DFT+U).
model_or_system: The physical system is the ultrathin VOx/MoSe2 heterostructure. The analysis models the magnetic behavior using both finite-cluster approximations and phenomenological models describing the collective dynamics based on oxide morphology.
key_observables: Magnetic moment enhancement, temperature dependence of magnetization ($M_s$) and coercivity ($H_c$), trion contribution in photoluminescence (PL), and charge transfer evidence from PL spectroscopy.
important_parameters: Oxide morphology (discontinuous clusters vs. continuous films), interfacial charge transfer magnitude, and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis distinguishes between the magnetic behavior of isolated VOx clusters and those forming continuous films. The use of QCM values for thickness is noted despite potential AFM discrepancies.
figures_summary: Figures show $	ext{MoSe}_2$ growth and $	ext{VO}_x$ deposition morphology (AFM/SEM). Spectroscopy (Raman/PL) confirms electronic changes, and VSM measures the magnetic hysteresis and temperature dependence, which are modeled theoretically.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents evidence: first, demonstrating interfacial charge transfer via PL/DFT; second, analyzing the magnetic enhancement due to this charge transfer; and finally, establishing that the collective magnetic response is dictated by the oxide's morphology, leading to a unified model.
why_interesting: The study provides a clear mechanism—interfacial charge transfer—to tune magnetism in 2D materials, which is highly relevant for designing novel spintronic and optoelectronic devices based on quantum materials.
